extracted.intended_audience: legal practitioners, agency staff, regulated entities, and members of the public who need to locate or comply with HHS regulations (Title 45, Subtitle A, Subchapter A)
extracted.subtask_description: An index/navigation page listing Parts 1–102 and their section headings for 45 CFR Subtitle A Subchapter A (General Administration), showing which parts contain standards, procedures, and criteria across HHS programs and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony by Employees and Production of Documents (Part 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope, purpose, and applicability; definitions; policy on presentation of testimony and production of documents; procedures when voluntary testimony is requested or when an employee is subpoenaed; subpoenas duces tecum; certification and authentication of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §2.1–§2.6 cover when employees may give testimony or produce documents in proceedings where the United States is not a party, including definitions, policies on presentation of testimony, procedures for subpoenas, and record authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct on NIH Federal Enclave (Part 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing conduct of persons and traffic on the NIH federal enclave, including general rules, traffic regulations, facilities/grounds, and penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–D (§3.1–§3.61) list general obligations, traffic regs (§3.21–§3.27), facilities and grounds (§3.41–§3.44), and penalties (§3.61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Process (Part 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for suits against the Department and its employees, other process directed to the Department or Secretary, process against officials in individual capacities, acknowledgement of mailed process, effect of regulations, materials related to petitions under the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program, and congressional subpoenas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §4.1–§4.7 define how legal process is served on HHS and its employees and the effect of such process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information Regulations (Part 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: General information about FOIA requests; how to request records; exemptions to disclosure; confidential commercial information; fees; appeals; and records retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–G (§5.1–§5.71) include procedural criteria for requesting records, claiming exemptions, fee structures (§5.51–§5.54), appeals (§5.61–§5.64), and retention policies (§5.71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act Regulations (Part 5b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions; purpose and scope; policy; maintenance of records; notification of or access to records; special procedures for access to medical records; correction/amendment procedures; appeals; disclosure of records; parents and guardians; exempt systems; contractors; fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §5b.1–§5b.13 set standards and procedural requirements implementing the Privacy Act for HHS systems of records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Inventions (Part 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who are employees; duty of employee to report inventions; determination as to domestic rights; option to acquire foreign rights; notice to employee of determination; employee's right of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §7.0–§7.8 establish reporting duties, rights determinations, foreign rights options, and appeals related to employee inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of HHS Research Facilities by Academic Scientists (Part 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose, policy, delegations of authority, criteria, and restrictions for use of HHS research facilities by academic scientists, engineers, and students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §9.1–§9.5 specify eligibility criteria and restrictions for external academic use of HHS research facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal and Utilization of Surplus Real Property (Part 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions, scope, general policies, limitations, awards, notice of available property, applications, assignment of surplus real property, general disposal terms and conditions, compliance with NEPA and related Acts, special terms, utilization, form of conveyance, compliance inspections and reports, and reports to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §12.1–§12.15 (and Exhibit A) lay out procedural and substantive requirements, including environmental compliance (NEPA) and application/process criteria for conveying surplus property for public health purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Federal Real Property to Assist the Homeless (Part 12a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions; applicability; general policies; expression of interest process; application process and requirements; action on approved applications; transfer documents; NEPA compliance; utilization and enforcement; and lack of administrative review rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §12a.1–§12a.15 describe eligibility, application and evaluation procedures, environmental review obligations, and enforcement for assisting the homeless with federal real property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of the Equal Access to Justice Act (Part 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions, information required from applicants, procedures for considering applications, including standards for entitlement to awards under the Equal Access to Justice Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–C (§13.1–§13.30) set out what applicants must provide and how agencies evaluate and decide fee-shifting awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures of the Departmental Grant Appeals Board (Part 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of what the part does; definitions; availability of procedures; summary; Board operation; representation; notice of appeal and Board response; preparation of an appeal file and written argument; record development; conferences; hearings; expedited process; powers; limitations on review; deadlines; parties; ex parte communications; mediation; calculation of deadlines; submission of material; record and decisions; timing of appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §16.1–§16.23 provide procedural standards and criteria for filing, developing, and deciding grant appeals before the Departmental Grant Appeals Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of Adverse Information to News Media (Part 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions, basic policy, precautions, regulatory investigations and trial-type proceedings, required context, advance notice, and retractions or corrections regarding release of adverse information to the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §17.1–§17.7 set standards for when and how adverse information may be released to the press and the safeguards to be observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Collection (Part 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; standards for administrative collection of debts; debt compromise; suspending and terminating collection activities; referrals to the Department of Justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–E (§30.1–§30.36) include procedural and substantive criteria for collecting debts owed to HHS, compromising debts, and referring matters to DOJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax Refund Offset (Part 31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and scope; definitions; general rule; certification and referral of debt; notice; review of Departmental records; review of a determination that a debt is past-due and legally enforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §31.1–§31.7 describe criteria and procedures for offsetting tax refunds to collect debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Wage Garnishment (Part 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and scope; definitions; general rule; notice; hearing; withholding order; certification by employer; amounts withheld; financial hardship; refunds; ending garnishment; right of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §32.1–§32.12 prescribe notice, hearing, hardship review, withholding procedures, and remedies for wage garnishment to collect debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary Offset (Part 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose, authority, scope; definitions; general rule; notice requirements before offset; review of department records; hearings; obtaining hearing official services; voluntary repayment agreements; special review; procedures for offset; offsets when Department is creditor or paying agency; interest, penalties, and administrative costs; non-waiver of rights; refunds; additional collection action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §33.1–§33.16 set procedural safeguards, notice and review standards, and calculation procedures for salary offset actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Filed Under the Military Personnel and Civilian Employees Act (Part 34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose and scope; definitions; filing procedures and time limits; allowable and unallowable claims; reconsideration or appeal; payment procedures; computation of award and settlement; claims involving carriers or insurers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §34.1–§34.9 provide substantive criteria and process rules for filing and adjudicating claims under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tort Claims Against the Government (Part 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions and procedures governing tort claims against HHS and the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–B (§35.1–§35.10) include procedural and substantive standards for presenting, investigating, and resolving tort claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects (Part 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic HHS policy for protection of human research subjects; additional protections for pregnant women, human fetuses, neonates, prisoners, and children involved in research; registration of Institutional Review Boards (IRBs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–E (§46.101–§46.505) set out standards for informed consent, IRB review, and additional protections for vulnerable populations and IRB registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange Visitor Program—Request for Waiver (Part 50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority; Exchange Visitor Waiver Review Board; policy; waivers for research and for delivery of health care services; procedures for submission of applications to HHS; personal hardship, persecution and visa extension considerations; compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §50.1–§50.8 provide criteria and procedures for requesting waivers of the two-year foreign residence requirement for exchange visitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Evaluating Comprehensive Plan to Reduce Reliance on Alien Physicians (Part 51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; application; who is eligible to apply; 'How will the plans be evaluated?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §51.1–§51.4 explicitly address the criteria and evaluation process for comprehensive plans submitted to reduce reliance on alien physicians; §51.4 focuses on evaluation standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer Services (Part 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability; definitions; volunteer service programs; acceptance and use of volunteer services; services and benefits available to volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §57.1–§57.5 specify eligibility, program operation, and acceptance criteria for volunteer services.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Practitioner Data Bank (Part 60)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; reporting of information; disclosure of information by the National Practitioner Data Bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts A–C (§60.1–§60.22) set standards for what must be reported, how data is handled, and disclosure criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Conduct (Part 73)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; conduct on the job; counter trafficking in persons requirements; gifts, travel, and employment; political activity; disciplinary action; reporting violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §73.101–§73.703 lay out ethics and conduct standards for HHS employees, including reporting and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial Actions Applicable to Letter of Credit Administration (Part 77)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; scope; conditions that may give rise to remedial actions; remedial actions; remedial action procedures; emergency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §77.1–§77.6 describe triggers and procedures for remedial actions in letter of credit administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Fraud Civil Remedies (Part 79)
rubrics_metrics.description: Basis and purpose; definitions; basis for civil penalties and assessments; investigation; review by reviewing official; prerequisites for issuing a complaint; complaint/answer/default; referrals to ALJ; notice of hearing; parties; separation of functions; ex parte contacts; disqualification; rights of parties; authority of ALJ; prehearing conferences; hearing; discovery; protective orders; sanctions; burden of proof; determining penalties; record; post-hearing briefs; initial decision; reconsideration; appeals; stays; judicial review; collection of penalties; administrative offset; deposit; compromise; limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §79.1–§79.47 provide a full enforcement and adjudicative framework with standards for investigations, proof, hearings, penalties, and appeals under the Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination Under Programs Receiving Federal Assistance (Part 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; application; discrimination prohibited; assurances required; illustrative application; compliance information; conduct of investigations; procedures for effecting compliance; hearings; decisions and notices; judicial review; effect on other regulations; definitions; appendices listing covered assistance and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §80.1–§80.13 (plus appendices) set civil-rights compliance standards, investigative and enforcement procedures, and assurance requirements under Title VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Hearings Under Part 80 (Part 81)
rubrics_metrics.description: General information; appearance and practice; parties; form, execution, service and filing of documents; time; proceedings prior to hearing; responsibilities and duties of presiding officer; hearing procedures; the record; posthearing procedures and decisions; judicial standards of practice; posttermination proceedings; definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §81.1–§81.131 supply procedural rules and evidentiary standards for hearings conducted under the nondiscrimination regulations in Part 80.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation for Enforcement of Sections 799A and 845 of the Public Health Service Act (Part 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purposes, definitions, coverage; discrimination in admissions prohibited; interim procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §83.1–§83.20 provide enforcement criteria and procedures related to specified sections of the Public Health Service Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability (Part 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; employment practices; accessibility; child care and education; postsecondary education; health/welfare/social services; general requirements; communications; web, mobile, and kiosk accessibility; accessible medical equipment; procedures; appendices with analyses and guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §84.1–§84.98 and appendices set accessibility standards, program requirements, and procedural rules for enforcement and compliance for recipients of HHS federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Handicap (Part 85)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; application; definitions; self-evaluation; notice; general prohibitions; employment; program accessibility for existing facilities and new construction; communications; compliance procedures; coordination and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §85.1–§85.62 describe enforcement procedures and program accessibility standards to ensure nondiscrimination on the basis of handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Sex (Part 86)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction; coverage; discrimination on the basis of sex in admission/recruitment; discrimination in education programs or activities; discrimination in employment in education programs; interim procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §86.1–§86.71 (and appendices) set criteria and procedures implementing Title IX for HHS-funded education programs and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Treatment for Faith-Based Organizations (Part 87)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions; applicability; faith-based organizations and Federal financial assistance; severability; appendices providing notices and model texts concerning beneficiary protections and award announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §87.1–§87.4 and appendices outline nondiscrimination and notice requirements applicable to faith-based organizations receiving HHS assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring HHS Funds Do Not Support Coercive or Discriminatory Policies (Part 88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; complaint handling and investigating; notice of Federal conscience and nondiscrimination laws; severability; appendix with model text of rights notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §88.1–§88.4 set complaint and investigation procedures and notice requirements to ensure HHS funds are not used to support coercive/discriminatory practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Integrity of Entities Implementing Leadership Act Programs (Part 89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability and requirements; definitions; organizational integrity of recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §89.1–§89.3 impose integrity, conflict-of-interest, and organizational standards on entities implementing certain HHS programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Age (Parts 90 & 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules on age nondiscrimination; what constitutes age discrimination; responsibilities of federal agencies; investigation, conciliation and enforcement procedures; standards for determining age discrimination; duties of HHS recipients; procedures for investigation, conciliation, and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts 90 (§90.1–§90.62) and 91 (§91.1–§91.50) set substantive and procedural criteria for preventing and remedying age discrimination in HHS-funded programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in Health Programs or Activities (Part 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; nondiscrimination provisions; specific applications to health programs and activities; procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §92.1–§92.304 provide standards and implementation guidance for nondiscrimination in health programs receiving federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Restrictions on Lobbying (Part 93)
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules; activities by own employees; activities by other than own employees; penalties and enforcement; exemptions; agency reports; appendices with certification and disclosure forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §93.100–§93.605 establish criteria for permitted and prohibited lobbying activities by recipients of federal funds, reporting requirements, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Prospective Contractors (Part 94)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; applicability; definitions; responsibilities of institutions regarding investigator financial conflicts of interest; management and reporting of financial conflicts of interest; remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §94.1–§94.6 set conflict-of-interest standards and institutional responsibilities for contractors and investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Administration—Grant Programs (Part 95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for states to file claims; cost allocation plans; automatic data processing equipment conditions for federal financial participation; equipment acquired under public assistance programs; general administration of grants to states (Parts 95.1–95.707) including financial provisions, reporting, and monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subparts and sections cover administrative, fiscal, and reporting standards for state-administered grant programs including conditions for FFP and reporting forms/instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block Grants (Part 96)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction; general procedures; financial management; direct funding of Indian tribes and tribal organizations; enforcement; hearing procedure; goals and program-specific provisions (e.g., SSBG, Low-income Home Energy Assistance, Community Services Block Grants, Substance Abuse Prevention/ Treatment Block Grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §96.1–§96.137 (and appendices) define eligibility, application, financial management, enforcement and hearing standards for block grant programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of Grants to the Insular Areas (Part 97)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of consolidated grant; which jurisdictions may apply; which grants may be consolidated; application process; award procedures; allowed uses of funds; fiscal, matching and administrative requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §97.10–§97.16 provide eligibility and procedural standards for consolidating grants to insular areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child Care and Development Fund (Part 98)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals, purposes, definitions; general application procedures; eligibility for services; program operations including parental rights and responsibilities; lead agency and provider requirements; use of funds; financial management; reporting requirements; Indian tribes; monitoring, non-compliance, and complaints; error rate reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §98.1–§98.102 specify programmatic, fiscal, eligibility, monitoring, and reporting standards for the Child Care and Development Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings for the Child Care and Development Fund (Part 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: General hearing provisions; preliminary matters such as notice and parties; hearing procedures; posthearing procedures and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §99.1–§99.33 establish procedural standards for adjudications under the Child Care and Development Fund rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental Review of HHS Programs and Activities (Part 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose; definitions; what programs and activities are subject; Secretary's obligation for federal interagency coordination; procedures for selection of programs and activities; communication with state and local officials; providing states an opportunity to comment on proposed federal financial assistance and direct federal development; receipt and response to comments; accommodating intergovernmental concerns; interstate obligations; simplification or consolidation of state plans; waiver authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §100.1–§100.13 define the process and criteria by which HHS communicates with and affords states/localities an opportunity to comment on federal actions — including how comments are received, considered, and responded to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Resources Priorities and Allocations System (HRPAS) (Part 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: General provisions; definitions; placement of rated orders; special priorities assistance; allocation actions; official actions; compliance; adjustments, exceptions, and appeals; miscellaneous provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §101.1–§101.93 (and appendices) set criteria and procedures for priority rating, allocation, compliance, and appeals under HRPAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment of Civil Monetary Penalties for Inflation (Part 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability; applicability date; penalty adjustment and table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections §102.1–§102.3 provide the method and effective dates for adjusting civil monetary penalty amounts for inflation.
